messages.subject: non-convergence with simulated data (N-mix)
parts:
Hello everyone,

i am analyzing data from brown hare spotlight counts (~140 sites with up to three counts each in spring and autumn) where sites left and entered the monitoring scheme. Over the last 20 years, the number of sites with data decreased from about 100 to 33. Although model fit as assessed by the Chi-squared discrepancy is not perfect (mean(out1$mean$fit) / mean(out1$mean$fit.new) =~ 2) models achieve convergence (Rhat-values < 1.1) with the field data.

To assess possible influence of the decreasing site pattern on accuracy and precision of the estimates, i set up simulations mimicking the features of the field data (data gaps in sites and repetitions). To this end, i adapted the Dail-Madsen simulator from AHM2 to account for variable survey area. Although density and detection probability estimates are reasonable, all models running on these simulated data indicate convergence failure but surprisingly good fit (fit/fit.new =~ 1).

Introduction of additional variance did not result in convergence and even led to convergence failure with the field data (which is counterintuitive given overdispersion, see attached). Also running the models for more iterations did not result in convergence with the simulated data. I am aware that the pattern of the simulated data is not exactly the same as in the field data (see attached) but can this be the reason?  

Any ideas why simulation models do not converge but the similar field data does?
Thanks in advance for any thoughts, (see code attached)
Tobias.
